excerpt: Secoda is an AI-powered data catalog, lineage and governance platform for data teams. Plans, funding and alternatives.
content:
Secoda is a data catalog and governance tool. Companies with a data warehouse and many dashboards use it so people can find the right table or metric, see where data comes from (lineage), check its quality and know who owns it. Its site now calls it the AI platform for data and analytics, and describes data cataloguing, lineage, observability and quality enriched with business context. An AI assistant lets people ask questions about company data in plain language.

Secoda was cofounded by Etai Mizrahi, its chief executive, and Andrew McEwen, and is backed by Y Combinator, among others. In September 2023 TechCrunch reported a $14 million round led by Craft Ventures, with Abstract Ventures and angel investors, which took its total funding to $16 million; BetaKit described it as a CAD 19 million Series A. Mizrahi said the money would go into engineering and research, and BetaKit reported that the company had shifted its product after the rise of large language models from a 'Google for data' search tool towards an AI copilot for data management.

Secoda's pricing page lists three plans without prices. Core includes column- and table-level lineage, the full data catalog, automations, API access, workspace analytics, SAML single sign-on and role-based access. Premium adds a Data Quality Score, guest accounts, policies, single-tenant deployment, PII scanning and VPC peering. Enterprise adds custom roles, self-hosted deployment, a dedicated account manager, access request management, SIEM logging and unlimited integrations. All plans route to the sales team.

Secoda suits data teams at growing companies that use a modern data stack (Snowflake, BigQuery, dbt, Looker and similar) and want a lighter catalog than the large enterprise options.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
